title: Buying first drum set and first job at a dollar and a quarter
summary: Saving from his St. Charles Hotel job he bought drums; John Perdonce got him his first gig.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Oh, by the way, is this... We talked to Mr. Glenny the other day and he said there was an old bass player. The first one he heard used to play with you. It was the first one that began picking. Perdonce? John Perdonce? John Perdonce? It might have been John Perdonce. Do you remember... By your time they were all picking a good deal, I guess. Yeah, everybody was picking. Yeah, everybody was picking that time. My time. So you started on drums just in the kitchen, you say. Then you didn't have a drum to start on.

No, so I went to work at St. Charles Hotel. I was running the freight elevator there. And I get paid every two weeks. So my mother knew I wanted to set a drum, so she said, well, let's put the money aside. So at one time I had enough to make a down payment. So we go over to Glenwall, where my father dealt that to me. And the sign-ups got me a set of drums. And the same evening I got the drums, John Perdonce heard about it. He didn't have a drum to play. He played somebody's fixin' run for us, some hardman or something, and they need a little music to play down on. Or set and rock and chart or somewhere down there. And that job paid a dollar quarter. And that was my first engagement. I was so happy to get that dollar quarter, because the dollar quarter would do a lot of money at that time. Was that a dance or? No, no, no, just was a ballet hoop, you know, a band ballet on the outside. We didn't play very long, about an hour or so.
What was Longhead Bob's last name?
